author: Henrique Almeida
description: Portugal’s Minister of Home Affairs Maria Lucia Amaral resigned late Tuesday after mounting criticism of the government’s handling of a series of deadly winter storms that have killed at least 14 people in recent weeks.
title: Portugal’s Home Affairs Minister Resigns After Deadly Storms

description: Rep. Marlin Stutzman (R-IN) discusses whether or not he believes the House will pass a vote on a tariff ban, and talks about how President Trump has utilized tariffs for the American economy. Stutzman also talks about the importance of supporting American ranchers, and his thoughts on Howard Lutnick’s testimony regarding the Epstein files. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Important Trump Has Tariffs As a Tool: Rep. Stutzman

author: Claire Jiao
description: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong will likely use his 2026 budget speech Thursday to position the nation as an artificial intelligence hub, a key facet of his government’s effort to diversify growth engines as global trade fractures.
title: Singapore’s Premier Wong Preps Budget for Age of AI, Trade Rifts

author: Emma Sanchez, Daniel Flatley, Joe Ryan
description: The US government issued a general license to allow oilfield-service companies to work in Venezuela as the Trump administration eases sanctions and pushes to rebuild the nation’s crude infrastructure.
title: US Allows Oilfield Contractors to Go to Work in Venezuelan Fields

author: Allyson Versprille
description: The head of the US Federal Aviation Administration said he expects Canada’s aviation regulator to move forward with approvals for Gulfstream jets after President Donald Trump threatened tariffs and other retaliatory actions against the country.
title: FAA Expects Canada to Announce Gulfstream Approvals This Week

author: Myles Miller
description: A House committee is escalating its investigation into a troubled Coast Guard shipbuilding program after accusing a major contractor of failing to turn over records related to years of delays and cost overruns, according to a letter from the panel’s chairman obtained by Bloomberg News.
title: House Scrutiny Escalates of Troubled Coast Guard Cutter Program

author: Steven T. Dennis
description: Democrats and Republicans are still negotiating immigration enforcement limits.
title: DHS Funding Deadline Approaches With No Deal Yet on Immigration

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss the latest economic data including the jump in US consumer delinquencies with Bloomberg Economics' Stuart Paul & Bloomberg Intelligence's Ira Jersey.  They continued this theme with Elizabeth Renter, NerdWallet Senior Economist. Also, Paul Andre Huet, America’s Gold & Silver Corporation Chairman & CEO & Gary Evans, United States Antimony Corp. Chair & CEO join to discuss their new joint venture in the light of President Trump's plan to launch a $12B minerals stockpile to counter China. Lastly Cheryl McKissack Daniel, McKissack & McKissack Chair of the Board, discusses economic perspectives and her new book on her family's legacy. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stock Rally Stalls as Bonds Climb on Retail Sales | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 2/10/2026

description: President Donald Trump is threatening to block the opening of a new bridge that connects Detroit to Windsor, Ontario until the US is given compensation and ownership of half of it. The Gordie Howe Bridge was expected to open to traffic soon. Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt talks about the issue at the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Threatens to Block Opening of Bridge to Canada

author: Naomi Ng, K Oanh Ha, Yang Yang (News), Eleanor Harrison-Dengate
description: Sanae Takaichi’s election gamble paid off. Now, the reality of governing begins. On today’s Big Take Asia: Unpacking the prime minister’s vision for Japan and hurdles ahead for her ambitious agenda.
title: Japan’s Takaichi Cements Power — But Can She Deliver on Her Promises?

description: Japan’s Sanae Takaichi just secured a landslide election win, with a majority that makes her the nation’s strongest postwar leader. What does this mean for her vision of a more assertive Japan? K. Oanh Ha and Sakura Murakami discuss on today’s Big Take Asia podcast.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Big Take Asia: How Takaichi’s Win Will Change Japan

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the funding fights on Capitol Hill for the Department of Homeland Security. On today's show, Republican Congressman Bryan Steil of Wisconsin, Democratic Congresswoman Suzan DelBene of Washington, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Democratic Congressman Joe Morelle of New York. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lawmakers Probe Fatal Minneapolis Shootings | Balance of Power: Early Edition 2/10/2026

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: The White House defended President Donald Trump’s decision to exclude two Democrats from a traditionally bipartisan dinner held for the nation’s governors later this month.
title: White House Defends Trump Snub of Democrats at Governors Dinner

author: Jimmy Jenkins
description: The FBI claims it seized ballots and voting records from a Georgia county election office in connection with a criminal investigation into alleged “improprieties” with the 2020 election.
title: DOJ Claims of ‘Improprieties’ Spurred Georgia Ballot Seizure

description: Congressman Joe Morelle, Democrat representing New York's 25th District and Ranking Member of the Committee on House Administration joins Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz to discuss the ongoing negotiations for a Homeland Security spending bill and there the two parties stand as its Friday deadline approaches. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Congress Far Away From DHS Funding As Deadline Nears

description: Congresswoman Suzan DelBene, Democrat from Washington and Chairwoman of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee joins Balance of Power to discuss how the House Democrats are targeting five more districts that favored President Donald Trump in the 2024 election, underscoring their confidence they can expand the pool of competitive districts in the November election. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Democrats Widen Battlefield District Targets on Pro-Trump Turf

description: Republican Representative Bryan Steil joins to discussed the  House GOP leaders delaying a procedural vote by seven hours Tuesday as some Republican members threatened to revolt over a leadership push to block politically tricky votes on President Donald Trump’s economic policies. As well as the looming funding lapse for the Department of Homeland Security Friday night unless Congressional Republicans, President Donald Trump and at least some Senate Democrats can find agreement on immigration enforcement. Or perhaps a plan to fund everything in the agency except ICE. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: House Rule Vote Delayed as GOP Threatens Revolt on Tariffs

description: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick acknowledged visiting Jeffrey Epstein at his private island in 2012 after Epstein was a convicted sex offender. But Lutnick told a Senate panel he has nothing to hide and "I have done absolutely nothing wrong." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lutnick Says He Met Epstein Three Times Over 14 Years

author: Magdalena Del Valle
description: The US and Iran each struck a positive tone about the start of diplomatic talks, though analysts remain skeptical that the engagement will be enough to head off US airstrikes.
title: New Iran Deal Distant Prospect as US Talks Drag, Airstrikes Loom

author: Kate Sullivan
description: Vice President JD Vance’s office said a now-deleted post that recognized the 1915 mass killings of Armenians as a genocide was sent in error.
title: Vance Removes Armenian ‘Genocide’ Post After Visit to Memorial

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Parliament is moving closer to approving a trade deal with the US after senior lawmakers agreed to make some changes ahead of a vote planned this month.
title: EU Lawmakers Advance US Trade Deal With Fresh Conditions

author: Alex Wickham, Ellen Milligan
description: As the dust settles on days of high-stakes political drama in Westminster, Labour insiders from across the party have arrived at a similar conclusion: sell Wes Streeting, hold Keir Starmer and buy Angela Rayner.
title: Buy Rayner and Sell Streeting, Say UK Labour Insiders as Drama Ebbs

description: As the US and Iran plan for another round of talks aimed at de-escalation, Israel’s Netanyahu plans to meet with Trump — and the threat of regional war continues to loom. Listen to Iran reporter Golnar Motevalli and host David Gura on the Big Take podcast. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Big Take: What’s At Stake For US-Iran Talks

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: The Pentagon is looking to turn President Donald Trump’s threats on government contractors into enforceable contract provisions and potentially Securities and Exchange Commission regulations.
title: Pentagon Seeks to Formalize Trump’s Threats on Contractor Pay

description: Analysts are expecting a strong quarter from Ford which reports earnings after the bell. President Donald Trump's push to cut subsidies for EVs and roll back emissions standards means Ford can sell gas-powered sport-utility vehicles and pickup trucks that generate huge profits. Keith Naughton reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fewer Regulations Expected to Help Power Ford Earnings

author: Myles Miller, Alicia Diaz
description: Senior US immigration officials told House lawmakers that officers involved in federal operations in Minnesota were trained on constitutional limits, crowd control and the use of force, as Congress scrutinizes two fatal shootings that occurred during enforcement actions earlier this year.
title: ICE, CBP Defend Training as Lawmakers Probe Minnesota Shootings

description: Cuba logged its first month without oil imports in a decade after Mexico halted all oil shipments to the fuel-starved country. Ivana Bargues has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Cuba Is in an Energy Crisis with No Oil Imports for the First Time in a Decade

author: Laura Nahmias
description: Lieutenant Governor Antonio Delgado suspended his campaign for governor of New York after deciding that he couldn’t defeat the incumbent, his fellow Democrat Kathy Hochul.
title: Democratic Challenger to NY Governor Hochul Suspends Campaign

description: Rep. Troy Downing (R) Montana states he doesn’t believe Congressional Democratic leaders are negotiating in good faith when it comes to the demands they are asking for. Downing expresses some doubt that Congress will avoid a shutdown by Friday, and voices his concerns with some of the reforms Democrats want for ICE agents. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Democrats Aren't Negotiating in Good Faith, Says Rep. Downing

author: Catherine Lucey, Matt Shirley
description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick minimized his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein Tuesday even as he acknowledged visiting the disgraced financier at his private island in 2012 after Epstein was a convicted sex offender.
title: Lutnick Downplays Relationship With Epstein in Senate Testimony

author: Stephan Kueffner
description: Ecuador prosecutors and police in a pre-dawn raid detained Guayaquil Mayor Aquiles Alvarez in connection with a money laundering and tax evasion probe.
title: Ecuador Police Detain Guayaquil Mayor in Money Laundering Probe

author: Leah Nylen
description: Federal enforcers have opened a consumer protection probe into the American Academy of Pediatrics and the leading professional association focused on transgender health care, extending the Trump administration’s attacks on transgender rights.
title: FTC Targets Medical Nonprofits in Trans Kids’ Health Probe

author: Nacha Cattan
description: Political organizer Analilia Mejia won the special Democratic primary in New Jersey’s 11th Congressional District, according to her rival, former Representative Tom Malinowski.
title: Mejia Rival Concedes in Special NJ House Democratic Primary

description: Harry Sideris, CEO of Duke Energy, says the company has signed new deals to power data centers with Microsoft and Compass Data Centers. He also talks about building grid reliability and working with the Trump administration. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Duke Energy Signs Deals to Power Data Centers With Microsoft, Compass

author: Julian Lee
description: Seaborne crude flows stable even as deliveries to India slump
title: Putin’s War Chest Drained by Big Discounts That Keep Oil Flowing

author: Derek Alberts, David Herbling
description: Kenya repatriated 27 of its citizens recruited to fight for Russia against Ukraine, the government said, as the families of 17 South African men fighting in that conflict demanded that President Cyril Ramaphosa intervene to bring them home.
title: Kenya Seals Return of Russia War Recruits as South Africans Wait

author: Swati Gupta
description: India tightened the rules governing social media content and their platforms, especially for artificially generated and manipulated material, according to a government gazette notification Tuesday.
title: India Cracks Down on AI-Generated Content on Social Media

author: Paul Vecchiatto
description: South Africa’s government plans to set up a new company to manage its vast property portfolio worth an estimated 155 billion rand ($9.75 billion).
title: South Africa Plans State Firm to Manage $9.8 Billion of Property

author: Selcan Hacaoglu, Firat Kozok
description: The transition of power is said to have become a prominent discussion topic within the governing AK Party.
title: Who Will Succeed Erdogan? Son’s Rising Profile Fuels Talk

author: Brad Stone
description: It’s time to move past the hysteria over wealth taxes and find a durable way forward.
title: How to Tax a Trillionaire

author: Alex Wickham
description: Keir Starmer thanked his cabinet for keeping him in his job and praised Labour’s Scottish leader, Anas Sarwar, a day after surviving his call for the prime minister to go.
title: Starmer Seeks to Heal Labour Rift After Surviving Day of Drama

author: Ewa Krukowska
description: The planned reform of the European Union’s carbon market should involve a slower annual pace of emissions reductions for industries from chemicals to cement, according to a member of the biggest political group in the bloc’s parliament.
title: EU Should Soften Caps in Emissions Market, Key Lawmaker Says

author: Maya Averbuch, Kelsey Butler
description: Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown and the fast-strengthening peso are putting additional pressure on Mexico’s economy by slowing the flow of money into the country.
title: Trump Immigration Policies, Peso to Drag Down Remittances

author: Alex Wickham
description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer is set to lose a third senior official from his government within days amid expectations that Cabinet Secretary Chris Wormald is preparing to resign, people familiar with the matter said.
title: Starmer to Lose Third Top Official With Wormald Expected to Quit

author: William Horobin
description: Francois Villeroy de Galhau’s exit as Bank of France governor creates a pivotal vacancy for both the country and the region at a sensitive time.
title: Villeroy Exit Sparks Race for Pivotal Bank of France Chief Role

author: Emily Birnbaum, Oma Seddiq
description: Silicon Valley’s richest venture capital firm emerges as a “lobbying juggernaut” for minimal AI regulation.
title: Andreessen Horowitz’s Rising Influence Over Trump-Era AI Policy

description: President Donald Trump said that Kevin Warsh, his pick to lead the Federal Reserve, can get the US economy to 15% growth and maybe even above that level during an interview with Fox Business. Tyler Kendall reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Sees 15% Economic Growth Under Fed Pick Warsh

author: Katarina Hoije
description: Sustained gunshots were heard on Tuesday in Conakry, the capital of Guinea in West Africa, according to news agencies.
title: Shooting Heard in Guinean Capital of Conakry, Agencies Report

author: Michael Sasso, Kriston Capps
description: The metro area has some of America’s highest rates of institutional home ownership, and local governments are pushing back
title: Atlanta Is Challenging Big Corporate Landlords Without Waiting on Trump

author: Alan Crawford
description: Investors and the voting public can only guess at the scale of the disruption ahead.
title: AI’s Great Upheaval Is Coming for Governments

author: Mohamed Omar Ahmed
description: Somalia’s federal lawmakers are debating amendments to the country’s provisional constitution in a bid to complete a long-delayed charter that would redefine how power is shared in the conflict-scarred Horn of Africa nation.
title: Somalia Lawmakers Weigh Changes to Federal Power Structure

author: Randy Thanthong-Knight, Suttinee (Ying) Yuvejwattana
description: For the first time in weeks, Thailand’s top cabinet ministers could breathe a sigh of relief as they gathered Tuesday at Government House in Bangkok.
title: Anutin’s Core Cabinet Team Intact After ‘Blue Wave’ Thai Vote

author: Zoe Tillman
description: US judges have halted the administration’s cuts to funding in more than half of 167 spending fights in the past year
title: Trump’s Grip on Billions of Taxpayer Dollars Loosened by Courts

author: Ott Tammik
description: Russia is exploiting negotiations to end the war in Ukraine as a “tool for manipulation” as it aims to restore relations with the US, but has no intention of ending the invasion, according to an assessment by Estonian foreign intelligence.
title: Russia Aims Only to ‘Buy Time’ in Peace Talks, Spy Report Says

author: Selcan Hacaoglu
description: Turkey would consider joining a regional nuclear arms race over concerns about Iran’s nuclear weapons ambitions, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said late Monday.
title: Turkey Says It Could Be Dragged Into Nuclear Arms Race Over Iran

author: Alberto Nardelli, Ewa Krukowska
description: Greece and Malta have emerged as the main obstacle to a European Union proposal to replace a Russian oil price cap with a ban on the services needed to ship the fuel.
title: Greece and Malta Hesitate Over EU’s Russia Oil Services Ban

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. 

On today's show, a White House official says the exact date in April for US President Trump to meet with Chinese leader, Xi Jinping, has not yet been finalized. It comes after Politico reported Trump would head to Beijing to meet Xi in the first week of April.

Keir Starmer shored up his position as UK prime minister during a dramatic day yesterday in Westminster that at times seemed like he might be forced to step down. The reprieve is likely only to be temporary.

Gucci sales fell in the final months of last year as Kering struggles to revive its biggest brand. Comparable revenue at Gucci tumbled 10% in the fourth quarter.

Today's guests: UK House of Lords member & pollster Robert Hayward, BNP Paribas Markets 360 Head of Developed Markets Rates Strategy & Economics, Europe Camille de Courcel & Canadian International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump-Xi April Meeting Date Not Finalized: White House Official | Daybreak Europe 2/10/2026

author: Antony Sguazzin
description: A South African court postponed the case against a state radio presenter accused of organizing the recruitment of people to fight for Russia against Ukraine for further investigation.
title: South Africa Delays Hearing of DJ Linked to Russia War Recruiting

author: Richard Bravo
description: French President Emmanuel Macron said the European Union needs to get tougher with US President Donald Trump, who is pushing for the “dismemberment” of the bloc.
title: Macron Says Europe Needs to Stand Up to Trump on Trade and Tech

author: Albertina Torsoli
description: French President Emmanuel Macron said Europe’s troubled next-generation fighter jet, the Future Combat Air System, must move forward in spite of squabbles between Dassault Aviation SA and Airbus SE over who should lead the program.
title: Macron Calls for Progress on Troubled European Fighter Jet

description: Keir Starmer shored up his position as UK prime minister during a dramatic day in Westminster that at times seemed like he might be forced to step down. The reprieve is likely only to be temporary. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Rosa Prince explains the situation. Her views are her own. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What's Next for UK's Starmer After PM Wins Reprieve?

author: Bilal Hussain, Sudipto Ganguly
description: Pakistan has agreed to play India at the T20 Cricket World Cup on Sunday, reversing an earlier boycott after intense diplomatic efforts by countries in the region.
title: Pakistan Reverses Plan to Boycott India Clash at T20 World Cup

author: Jenni Marsh
description: After pro-democracy protests rocked Hong Kong in 2019, mainland China tightened its grip by imposing a broad national security law on the former British colony. Since then, dozens of opposition figures have been arrested, including Jimmy Lai, a former media tycoon and pro-democracy campaigner. On Feb. 9, Lai, 78, was sentenced to 20 years in prison after being found guilty of national security crimes in a trial that demonstrated Chinese President Xi Jinping’s resolve to stamp out political disse
title: How the Security Law Used Against Jimmy Lai Has Changed Hong Kong

author: Weilun Soon
description: The US Treasury Department has requested information from Adani Enterprises Ltd. related to allegations in a news report that the company imported Iranian oil products into India.
title: Adani Enterprises Says Working With US in Iran Sanctions Probe

author: Yoshiaki Nohara
description: Japanese Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick will meet this week to discuss the first project to be funded via the $550 billion investment vehicle that was a pillar of the two countries’ trade deal last year.
title: Akazawa, Lutnick to Discuss First Project for $550 Billion Fund

author: Robert Burnson
description: US Attorney General Pam Bondi asked an appeals court to resurrect the scuttled indictments of two of President Donald Trump’s perceived enemies, former FBI director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James.
title: Bondi Seeks to Revive Criminal Indictments of Comey, James

author: Yian Lee
description: Bank of America Corp. significantly boosted its prediction for Taiwan’s economic growth this year, adding to a slew of upgrades even after a rip-roaring 2025 propelled by AI demand.
title: BofA Nearly Doubles Taiwan 2026 GDP Forecast on ‘Relentless’ AI

author: Chandra Asmara
description: Indonesia’s army is preparing up to 8,000 troops for a possible peacekeeping mission in Gaza, underscoring President Prabowo Subianto’s push for the world’s largest Muslim-majority nation to take on a bigger role in international security.
title: Indonesia Weighs Sending Up to 8,000 Troops for Gaza Peace Plan

author: Nectar Gan
description: China signaled greater efforts to protect national security in Hong Kong after the sentencing of Jimmy Lai renewed foreign governments’ calls for the former media mogul’s release.
title: China to Deepen HK Security Focus as Jimmy Lai Case Stirs Outcry

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Troy Downing (R) Montana discusses if the government will shut down later this week and voices his concerns with some of the reforms Democrats want for ICE agents. Sarah Krissoff, former federal prosecutor for the Southern District of New York, discusses the Department of Justice’s mishandling of Jeffrey Epstein files by keeping the documents redacted when members of Congress were told the files would be unredacted.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lawmakers Review Epstein Documents at DOJ | Balance of Power: Late Edition 02/09/2026

author: Alicia Diaz, Matt Shirley
description: House Republicans on Monday advanced a procedural motion to block a vote on President Donald Trump’s tariff agenda, potentially delaying a politically uncomfortable vote on his most prominent economic policy until at least July.
title: House Republicans Move to Keep Putting Off Vote on Trump Tariffs

author: Maia Spoto
description: California may not enforce its mask ban against federal immigration agents, a Los Angeles federal judge ruled Monday, though she left intact other provisions in new state laws requiring officers to identify themselves.
title: Enforcement of California’s ICE Mask Ban Blocked by Judge

author: Irina Anghel
description: Things ought to be looking rosy for Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who began the year begging a dissatisfied public to judge him on his ability to turn around the UK economy.
title: Starmer Is Helming an Economic Revival He May Not Get to Enjoy

author: Niki Koswanage, Tom Redmond
description: Malaysian anti-corruption chief Azam Baki held millions of shares in a financial-services company, a corporate filing shows, the first public disclosure of a major stake in his name since an uproar over his shareholdings several years ago spurred protests calling for him to step down.
title: Malaysian Anti-Graft Chief Returns to Stock Market After Outcry
